request-journey.title: A 200 response can still fail the lesson contract
request-journey.summary: The real loopback lab stops at body validation; DNS and TLS remain separate model or extension boundaries.

nodes.label: Name/address
nodes.description: Offline DNS model or an already known loopback address.

nodes.label: Decode and validate
nodes.description: Bounded content, media type, syntax and fields.

nodes.label: Publish valid lesson
nodes.description: Only compatible observations become application results.

steps.title: Locate the failure stage
steps.explanation: Name resolution and endpoint connectivity are distinct checks.

steps.title: Observe response semantics
steps.explanation: An HTTP response proves an exchange occurred, not that its lesson data is correct.

steps.title: Reject malformed success
steps.explanation: The /bad-json route returns 200 but must fail decoding.

steps.title: Accept compatible content
steps.explanation: No TLS, browser authorization or public-service claim follows from this local result.

timeouts.title: The caller stops waiting; the server still needs cleanup
timeouts.summary: An Event confirms the local server received the request before the controlled header wait expires.

nodes.label: Client sends /stall
nodes.description: Client owns a short bounded socket wait.

nodes.label: Server readiness event
nodes.description: The handler has received the request.

nodes.label: Release and join
nodes.description: Fixture releases the handler and closes listener/threads.

steps.title: Confirm receipt
steps.explanation: A refusal would be a different test; readiness proves this route started.

steps.title: Observe bounded waiting
steps.explanation: Timeout means the client stopped waiting, not that server processing was rolled back.

steps.title: Clean owned resources
steps.explanation: Always release the handler and close the server, including failed assertions.
